entries.title: Draft: exact crossing factorization through a series corridor
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent mathematical review pending. Let two disjoint finite chamber graphs L and R be joined only by a simple k-edge path from u in L to v in R. Its interior vertices have degree two. Under independent Bernoulli(p) bonds, 0<p<1, and without external or cross-chamber identifications, terminals S in L and T in R satisfy P(S connects T)=p^k P_L(S connects u) P_R(v connects T)<=p^k. The bound is attained when S={u} and T={v}. Every path edge is a separating bridge; the three necessary and sufficient events use disjoint independent edge families. This is an auxiliary finite-graph result and does not solve square-lattice conformal invariance.
assumptions: Only the stated corridor joins the chambers
Product bond law; no external connectivity

entries.title: Draft counterexample: unmarked geometric convergence does not preserve crossings
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent mathematical review pending. For n>=81 put t=floor(sqrt(n)), a=t, b=2t+1, k=t+1, and m=floor(n/2). Let D_n be the interior of the union of the rectangles [0,a/n]x[0,1], [b/n,1]x[0,1], and [a/n,b/n]x[(m-1/2)/n,(m+1/2)/n]. Each D_n is a simply connected Jordan polygon with fixed corner marks A=(0,1), B=(0,0), C=(1,0), D=(1,1). Its closure Hausdorff distance from the closed unit square is <=k/(2n), its boundary Hausdorff distance is <=b/n, its area loss is k(n-1)/n^2, and its unmarked Caratheodory kernel at (1/2,1/2) is the open unit square. Yet in the induced nearest-neighbor graph on mesh-1/n vertices in its closure, independent bonds p=1/2 give P(AB connects CD)<=2^-k, tending to zero: only the row y=m/n joins the chambers. Canonical square crossings are uniformly positive by classical RSW. The missing marked-prime-end convergence is essential; this example refutes an overstrong approximation bridge, not the properly marked C0017 target.
assumptions: Source AB is x=0; sink CD is x=1
Geometric convergence is unmarked; marked prime ends need not converge

entries.title: Draft: distinct Euclidean corner marks can collapse conformally
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent mathematical review pending. For n>=81 put t=floor(sqrt(n)), a=t, b=2t+1, m=floor(n/2) and form the Jordan domain D_n from [0,a/n]x[0,1], [b/n,1]x[0,1], and the corridor [a/n,b/n]x[(m-1/2)/n,(m+1/2)/n], taking the interior of their union. Normalize the disk Riemann map f_n by f_n(0)=(1/2,1/2), f_n'(0)>0. Its Jordan boundary extension satisfies |f_n^{-1}(0,1)-f_n^{-1}(0,0)|<=8/n. The boundary arc containing both corners lies behind a height-1/n gate at x=b/n. Brownian motion must hit this gate before exiting on that arc. The half-plane Poisson kernel bounds its harmonic measure by 1/[pi*n*(1/2-b/n)]<=4/(pi*n); the preimage arc has angular length <=8/n. Thus Euclidean corner convergence, even with unmarked kernel and boundary Hausdorff convergence, does not imply marked-prime-end convergence.
assumptions: Brownian harmonic measure and its conformal invariance

entries.title: Draft warning: refuted unmarked crossing-preservation bridge
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof, independent mathematical review pending. The following auxiliary assertion is refuted by the boundary-neck construction: closure Hausdorff convergence, boundary Hausdorff convergence, area convergence, unmarked Caratheodory convergence to a fixed Jordan domain, and Euclidean convergence of four distinct boundary marks are sufficient to preserve critical square-lattice crossing probabilities of the marked arcs. These conditions alone do not control marked prime ends. This is a record of a false proposed bridge, not a theorem and not a refutation of conformal invariance for correctly marked approximations.
assumptions: This entry describes a refuted auxiliary assertion
No promotion to a theorem or a parent-problem solution

relations.rationale: The construction has exactly k mandatory corridor edges; its probability bound uses the exact series factorization.
It meets all five geometric and Euclidean-mark conditions while crossing tends to zero instead of the canonical square lower bound.
The gate and the trapped boundary arc are exactly those of the explicit Jordan neck family.
The 8/n boundary-preimage estimate identifies the omitted marked-prime-end hypothesis in the false bridge.
